issues.legal_issue: Failure to comply with every mandatory mode of publishing a preliminary land-acquisition notification invalidates the acquisition proceedings from the objection stage onward, notwithstanding individual notice or actual awareness.
material_facts: The acquisition notification appeared in two daily newspapers, but neither publication satisfied the requirement that at least one newspaper be in the regional language.
A corrigendum enlarging the area proposed for acquisition was not published in any newspaper.
The landowners had not filed objections within the prescribed period, and the authorities relied on individual notices and the landowners’ awareness of the acquisition proceedings.
issues.conclusion: The prescribed publication requirements were mandatory and had not been strictly complied with. Individual notice or awareness did not cure the defects. The acquisition proceedings were properly quashed from the objection stage onward, and the landowners were permitted to submit further objections.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 4(1)(a)–(c) and 5-A of the Jammu and Kashmir Land Acquisition Act, the prescribed methods of publishing a preliminary notification must all be strictly followed; none may be omitted or waived, and individual notice or actual awareness does not replace statutory publication. Because the Act affects landowners’ rights, these requirements are strictly construed. The Court relied on Khub Chand v. State of Rajasthan, which held that mandatory publication requirements must be obeyed and non-compliance invalidates the ensuing proceedings; Syed Hasan Rasul Numa v. Union of India, which reiterated that publication by only some required methods is insufficient; and Kunwar Pal Singh v. State of U.P., which held that all prescribed modes of publication must be used.

predicates.land_acquisition_proceeding: The authorities initiated a proceeding to acquire land for a public purpose.
predicates.required_publication_modes_not_all_compl: The authorities failed to use every legally prescribed mode of publishing the acquisition notification, including any required publication of a corrigendum.

issues.definition: In a land-acquisition proceeding, if the authorities fail to complete every required publication mode, the acquisition proceedings are invalid from the objection stage onward.
